//: THE DISPENSED CUP.  SCP-294 puts out a paper drinking cup; item::fill_with is what actually fills it, and it caps the pour by whichever of the cup's volume or weight runs out first, so both limits are simply the ceiling the machine fills up to.  CDDA needs nothing special to stop the cup being eaten by its contents - a container is only corroded through a liquid's own drop_action, and none of these liquids carry one.
//2: WHY 500 ML AND NOT THE ARTICLE'S 12 OZ (355 ML).  Two rounds of the regression test in tests/scp_294_test.cpp drove this.  A 355 ml cup could not hold whole CHARGES of a fair number of real liquids, because some are defined at 400-500 ml per charge (bark tea, bee's knees, three sisters stew, baked beans, the fermentable mixtures, electrolyte slurry): charges are indivisible, so the machine produced nothing for a perfectly ordinary drink.  500 ml is the capacity the base game's own drink cup uses (styrofoam_cup), and at that size only genuinely unpourable batch items remain (a couple of 10 L-per-charge chemistry intermediates), which the machine refuses gracefully instead of erroring.  The cup is oversized on purpose, though: the machine pours ONE SERVING (250 ml) into it, never a full cup - see scp_294_serving_volume in src/scp_294.cpp.
//3: THE WEIGHT LIMIT IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME BUG, and it must not be set to 'a drink'.  It was 1 kg, which silently broke the dense liquids: 'cup of gold' is 2500 g for a single charge and a 250 ml serving of mercury is ~3.4 kg, so the pour was rejected and the machine produced nothing - surfacing as an on-screen debugmsg error dialog.  The machine now fills the cup with item::fill_with, which caps the pour by BOTH remaining volume and remaining weight, so this limit is simply the ceiling it fills up to.  10 kg sits comfortably above the densest real liquid (mercury) while stopping a very fine-grained liquid from pouring an absurdly heavy cup.
description: A plain white paper drinking cup, faintly warm, with a ring of small print near the rim that resolves into no language at all when you try to read it.

//: 'A CUP OF JOE'.  The one request the article warns about: the machine reads the phrase literally and draws the fluid from the person standing in front of it.  Non-lethal here - it costs a great deal of blood and the memory of your own face going grey, not your life.
description: It is warm and it is red and it is not coffee.  There is tissue in it.  You are fairly sure, without checking, whose it is.

//: 'A CUP OF GOLD'.  The article's wording is exact: the machine dispenses MOLTEN gold, which is why this is a hazard and not a payday - it is priced at nothing, so it is not a currency faucet, and handling it burns.  The temperature is fiction, the burn is not.
//2: IT COOLS.  The machine retrieves matter (addendum 294m: an equal amount vanished from the sealed container 25 m away), so it does not also keep that matter hot forever - once it is in your hands, ordinary physics resumes and the gold sets.  Mechanically that is a countdown: the item is already active because EVERY comestible without NO_TEMP is created active - item::has_temperature() is 'is_comestible() && !NO_TEMP' (src/item.cpp:3190-3192) and the item constructor sets active = true on that branch (src/item.cpp:257-259) - and the expiry runs countdown_action inside if( active ) (src/item.cpp:4770-4785).  Comestibles are processed every 10 minutes (src/item.cpp:4183-4184), so a '10 minutes' countdown sets the gold somewhere in the 10-20 minute range.
//3: DO NOT ADD SPAWN_ACTIVE HERE.  An earlier version carried it, on the false assumption that it was what activated the item - a live save showed the OTHER comestibles in this file stored as active = true with no such flag, and the constructor above explains why.  item::activate() early-returns when already active (src/item.cpp:481-483), so the flag was harmless, but it was dead weight and the comment claiming it was load-bearing was wrong.
description: A cup of gold the way the earth makes it: white-hot, flowing, throwing a light that does not move like firelight.  The paper cup does not care.  You should.

countdown_action.msg: The gold in the cup dulls, thickens, and stops moving.  It is a lump of metal now.

//: COOLED GOLD - what one serving of molten gold becomes once it sets.  Mass is conserved from the pour (one 250 ml charge of scp_294_molten_gold, 2500 g) while the volume drops to ~130 ml, because solid gold is far denser than the liquid the machine dispensed.
//2: THE WEIGHT HERE IS A LITERAL, AND THAT MAKES IT A COUPLING.  The pour is computed at runtime - one serving, via item::fill_with (src/scp_294.cpp) - so this number and that pour have to agree.  tests/scp_294_test.cpp enforces it: the test mirrors the machine, sums the mass actually poured, and checks it against this item, so changing the serving size, the cup, or the molten gold's own weight fails loudly instead of silently desyncing.
//3: PRICED LIKE BASE GOLD, ON PURPOSE.  CDDA deliberately makes gold worthless after the Cataclysm - gold_small is price_postapoc '0 cent' with the comment 'scrap gold is actually worthless', and a 1 L gold ingot is '1 USD' ('novelty item, absolutely useless') - and trading uses the practical price (item::price(true), src/item.cpp:1921-1928).  So this is a curiosity, not a payout.  Its use is that it reduces back to gold_small, which feeds every recipe that wants gold.
description: A heavy, dull-yellow lump, still faintly warm, with the smooth sag of something that was poured rather than cast.  It looks exactly like what it is.

//: 'LIQUID NITROGEN' / 'NITROGEN'.  There is no liquid-nitrogen item in the base game (the only nitrogen item is a compressed gas), so the machine needed one of its own.  On consumption it does what liquid nitrogen does.
description: It boils without heat and frosts the outside of the cup it is somehow not freezing.  The air above it turns to slow white smoke and stays there.

//: 'CUP OF CARBON'.  The companion test to 'diamond': the machine will not pour liquid carbon FOR a diamond, but it will pour liquid carbon when asked for carbon.  Inert, and mostly a curiosity.
description: Black and glossy and impossibly hot, and yet it moves like cold oil.  Nothing in the cup is burning.  That is the part you cannot stop looking at.

//: 'A CUP OF MUSIC'.  Abstract request, abstract result - the article's subject 'felt', rather than heard, a continuous rhythm, and could move with a fluidity he had not had before.  Modelled as a short-lived status.
description: Clear and sparkling and faintly alcoholic, and it does not taste of anything so much as it keeps time.  Somewhere behind your sternum something has begun, patiently, to count.

//: 'MY LIFE STORY'.  Viscous, opaque, black, and the article says Dr.████████ remembered everything that had ever happened to him.  Here it is a memory effect, not a written item - the payoff is the remembering.
description: Opaque and black and far heavier than it should be, slow as syrup, and it smells of the inside of a house you have not thought about in years.

//: 'A CUP OF PERTINENT MEDICAL KNOWLEDGE'.  Clear green; the article's agent could suddenly practise Foundation medicine.  Modelled as a temporary status - the agent in the article lost the knowledge again afterwards, which is exactly what a timed effect is for.

name.str_sp: a cup of pertinent medical knowledge

description: Perfectly clear and perfectly green, and cold in a way that seems to be about you rather than about the liquid.  It goes down like water and sits in you like a textbook you have already read.

//: 'THE PERFECT DRINK'.  The article is unambiguous about the cost: the subject drank it, identified it as something he had wanted his whole life and then could not have again, and killed himself.  That is a psychological wound, not a lethal one - per this mod's handling of horror, this is a SEVERE debuff (a morale floor and a long despair status), never a forced death.
description: Odourless, and the colour of lavender, and it is not any one drink so much as the memory of the best one you will ever have.  The cup is warm.  You are not sure you want to finish it, and you are certain you will.

//: 'THE BEST DRINK I'VE EVER HAD'.  The machine cannot read a mind, but it can do the next best thing: pick a strong drink and let the fiction carry the rest.  High fun, no strings.

name.str_sp: a drink you have had before

description: Dark, with a smell underneath the cola that you can almost place - a bar, a night, people who are probably not alive now.  It tastes exactly the way you remember it tasting, which is the unnerving part.

//: 'SURPRISE ME'.  The article's punchline: normal water, heated to about 200 C; the vibration of being carried turns it to steam and sprays boiling water over a two-metre radius.  Here it scolds the drinker and scalds the hand that takes it.
description: It looks like water and it is water, and it is the single most dangerous thing in the cup, because it has been heated far past the point where water is willing to stay water.
